html:
The discovery of a rich new vein of silver at the mines of Laurion, in southern Attica, in 483 BCE. The windfall belonged to the Athenian state.

Some wanted to share it out among the citizens. Themistocles persuaded the assembly to spend it on a fleet instead, pointing to the war with the island of Aegina, though he likely had Persia in mind. Herodotus says Athens built 200 warships, the fast oared triremes of the age.

Three years later, in 480 BCE, those ships won the Battle of Salamis against the fleet of Xerxes. The navy made Athens a sea power, led the Delian League, and gave political weight to the poor citizens who rowed it.

Laurion's silver also became the owl coins trusted across the Mediterranean. The mines were worked by thousands of slaves in harsh conditions, the hidden cost of Athenian wealth.
sum: The discovery of a rich new vein of silver at the mines of Laurion, in southern Attica, in 483 BCE. The windfall belonged to the Athenian state.
